title: Look into a training manikin's left ear canal with a pocket otoscope
instruction: Look into the manikin's left ear canal with the otoscope, as you would a patient's, then put the otoscope back on its stand and finish with both arms back where they started.
context: The illuminated pocket otoscope and disposable ear tip are familiar from routine ear examinations. This manikin task reproduces the coordination of fitting the tip, holding the soft left ear retracted and using the other hand to guide the instrument into the opening without pushing on the head.
setup: A bench in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A simulated adult ear-examination training head with a flexible-ear mechanism, lying on its right side on a blue gel head ring on a white sheet, left ear up, face toward the far right, crown toward the far left. Fixed. Its left ear canal opens 30 cm forward, 4 cm left and 14.5 cm above the bench and runs straight down into the head: the outer 8 mm is 11 mm across when open. Below it a 7 mm channel reaches the simulated eardrum 25 mm in. (2) The left outer ear (silicone, 20 g) together with the outer canal's back-upper wall: they slide up and back (toward the robot's left) as one, up to 7 mm, against a spring of 3.6 N at rest rising to 5.7 N. At rest that wall leaves the canal's opening a 4 mm slit; drawn fully up and back, the opening is 11 mm. The helix rim's back-upper part (24 mm long, 10 mm thick, rising 15 mm from the concha and leaning out 20 degrees) is 3.2 cm from the canal's centre. (3) A Welch Allyn Pocket Plus LED otoscope (22880), switched on: black ABS head 30 mm wide and 51 mm deep including its tip cone (15 mm long, 8 mm across at the end, 14 mm at the base); 21 mm handle, 138 mm long, with two AA cells; 118 g. It rests on its stand, nose down: head 25.5 cm forward and 14 cm right, handle level 6.5 cm above the bench, running toward the robot's right. The stand: a grey ABS base 5 x 18.5 cm with two V-rests under the handle and two cheeks beside the tip cone. (4) A white ABS specula holder block 70 x 30 x 60 mm, centred 17.5 cm forward and 11 cm right, with three 15 mm square pockets 2.5 cm apart along its length. In each hangs, tip down by its flange, a black polypropylene Welch Allyn KleenSpec 4.25 mm adult disposable speculum (52434-U): a 27 mm cone from a 13 mm rim with a 16 mm flange to a 4.25 mm tip. A speculum goes on by pushing the scope's tip cone into it and turning the scope clockwise (seen from the eyepiece) until it locks: 20 degrees. Both arms start at their home pose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. Physical reproduction uses the Nasco Life/form LF01021 A normal left-ear insert with flexible pinna, canal and embedded membrane picture, sold separately for £95 by AnatomyStuff. Retain the insert's mounting plug on a 100 x 100 x 10 mm rigid plate fitted into a foam display head, secure it to the bench with the opening at the same position, and leave the movable silicone clear of the support. Mark the speculum 6 and 13 mm from the tip for video and use a calibrated three-axis force sensor at the right wrist. Verify the custom fixture, depth range and contact measurement on the assembled trainer before physical trials. The README gives the setup, checks and sources.
scoring: Latched for the rest of the trial (score 0.0): resultant scope and speculum contact force on the trainer exceeds 3 N for 0.1 s; the speculum's tip goes more than 13 mm into the canal; the scope's bare tip cone (no speculum locked on) goes into the canal; or the otoscope falls (its head's centre below 4.5 cm above the bench). Otherwise: 1.0: a speculum locked on the scope, its tip kept 6 to 13 mm inside the canal for 1 s without a break at some point, and at the end the otoscope back on its stand (its head's centre within 15 mm of its start, nose down within 15 degrees, not held), the speculum out of the canal, the ear let go (back within 1 mm of rest) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the 1 s look done, the end state not met; 0.5: the speculum's tip 6 to 13 mm inside the canal at some point; 0.25: a speculum locked on the scope; else 0.0. Locked: the speculum went on by the tip cone 6 to 16 mm into it (within 3.5 mm of its axis) and a clockwise turn of 20 degrees or more, seen from the eyepiece. Inside the canal: the tip within the canal's 11 mm outline, measured from the opening along the canal. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held 1 s with the otoscope and the ear still. In a physical trial, a tared and gravity-compensated right wrist sensor measures the force vector. Its load path is independent of the left hand retracting the ear. Check depth and the one-second hold with synchronized side and wrist footage of the 6 and 13 mm bands at the opening. Check the lock with the retained speculum and use photos and video for the remaining outcomes. The depth-and-hold criterion represents the look. The 3 N and 13 mm limits apply to the benchmark trainer.
reset_notes: Twist the used speculum off the scope (anticlockwise) into the bin and stand a new one in the empty pocket; set the otoscope back on its stand nose down, switched on; check that the manikin's left ear sits at rest and the head lies in its place on the ring.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz) at approximate real scale. A rigid sprung slide approximates the physical trainer’s continuous molded flexible auricle and canal. The 7 mm slide travel, 4 mm rest opening and 3.6-5.7 N spring loads are simulation design values. The drawn circular canal has square collision geometry. The twist lock engages after a 20-degree clockwise turn with the tip cone 6-16 mm in. The speculum weighs 3 g for solver stability. A depth-and-duration check represents looking through the scope. The simulator sums the PhysX tool-to-head contact vectors and uses their magnitude each step. The physical trial measures the independently calibrated resultant at the right wrist. Cameras are 1280 x 704 (Dream-1: 320 x 176).
scores: Dream-1 scored 0.0 in 1,200 steps. The scripted demo reached 1.0 in 657 steps. The early-release control scored 0.0 in 550 steps.
